map.五十音图是日语发音基础：清音 45 音加拨音 ん，共 46 个基础清音；本工具当: The kana chart is the foundation of Japanese pronunciation: 45 plain sounds plus the syllabic nasal ん make 46 base sounds. This tool currently covers only these 46 plain sounds; voiced, semi-voiced and digraph sounds are not included yet. Clicking a card calls SpeechSynthesis to read it aloud (the browser needs a Japanese voice; when unsupported, the romanization is shown instead).

map.あ行 a/i/u/e/o、か行 ka/ki/ku/ke/ko… 共 46 基础音: a-row a/i/u/e/o, ka-row ka/ki/ku/ke/ko... 46 base sounds in total (including ん); hiragana derives from cursive Chinese characters and katakana from their radicals, e.g. ア comes from the left-ear component of a Chinese character.
map.か行加浊点成 が ga/ぎ gi/ぐ gu/げ ge/ご go；拗音 きゃ ky: Adding voicing dots to the ka-row gives が ga/gi/gu/ge/go; digraphs such as きゃ kya, きゅ kyu and きょ kyo are formed from a consonant plus a small ya-row kana. The practice area here covers only the 46 plain sounds; use these rules to study voiced and digraph sounds on your own.
map.平假名片假名用哪个？: When Do You Use Hiragana and When Katakana?
map.平假名用于本土词/语法、片假名用于外来语/拟声；二者同音不同形，需都认。: Hiragana covers native words and grammar, katakana covers loanwords and onomatopoeia. The two sound the same but look different, so recognize both.
map.为什么是五十音不是五十？: Why Is It Called Fifty Sounds Rather Than Fifty?
map.清音 45 + ん = 46，传统称「五十音」含历史全表；实际基础发音 46 个: 45 plain sounds plus ん makes 46. The traditional name gojuon refers to the historical full chart, while the actual base pronunciation is 46 sounds, extended by voiced, semi-voiced and digraph sounds.
